newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DECISIVE GAME FOR RELEGATION DUO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DECISIVE GAME FOR RELEGATION DUO.

text.p: While Manchester United can move six points clear of Liverpool at the top if they beat Derby on Saturday, the crunch game in the English premier league is the relegation duel between Nottingham Forest and Southampton.
Between them they have occupied one of the three relegation positions since September and know that another defeat would make survival that much harder to achieve.
Forest are currently 18th with 31 points, with only Coventry (30) and Southampton (27) beneath them.

While those three occupy the bottom spots, Middlesbrough (32), Sunderland (33) and West Ham (33) are all within striking distance -- and safety. But defeat for Forest or Southampton will make their position that much more vulnerable.
At least Forest caretaker player-coach Stuart Pearce has a fully fit squad to pick from.
Welsh international goalkeeper Mark Crossley will play despite back and hernia problems, while midfielder Chris Bart-Williams (knee) and striker Kevin Campbell (hamstring) have resumed training.

Southampton, without a win in their last five league games, are desperate for the points to move off the foot of the table but coach Graeme Souness will be without suspended Dutch defender Ken Monkou.
At least he is able to recall Matt Le Tissier who has recovered from a foot injury.
The teams drew 2-2 at Southampton earlier in the season, but both have struggled for any kind of consistency.

Forest enjoyed a brief resurgence after Pearce replaced Frank Clark as caretaker manager in December, but since then their results have been disappointing with just one win in their last 10 league games -- the last four of which have been drawn.

Dutch international Pierre van Hooydonk has yet to score in four matches since his 4.5 million pounds ($7.0 million) move from Celtic, but fellow striker Dean Saunders says their partnership is beginning to blend.
"Also, we have our destiny in our own hands still," he added. "If we win our three remaining home matches then we will stay up. I think if Southampton lose on Saturday they will be relegated."

With Middlesbrough playing in the League Cup final against Leicester on Sunday, Sunderland travelling to rivals Newcastle and Derby facing an in-form Manchester United at Old Trafford, Forest could improve their hopes with a victory. Nothing else will really do for them.
At the other end, if Manchester United beat Derby as expected they will gain a six-point lead over second-placed Liverpool at least until Sunday when Liverpool play Coventry.
Arsenal could keep their slim title chances alive if they win the London derby at Chelsea which has a Saturday morning kickoff.
